passage:
I'm Minakshi, and being in the middle is funny. Everyone is very nice to you, right until they aren't.

Last term Bhavna and Deepa stopped speaking over a borrowed laptop charger, or really over what the charger meant. Bhavna sat on my bed one night and said, "You saw how she treated me, right?" The next day Deepa cornered me: "Tell me what she said about me." My stomach twisted, because part of me wanted to please whoever was in the room.

I told each of them the same thing. "I won't carry messages. I care about you both, and honestly the charger seems small next to the friendship, but I'm not going to pick a side." Bhavna stormed off. Deepa called me useless. It hurt 😔.

A month later they each told me, separately, that they trusted me because I never repeated what they'd said.

qa.q: What did Bhavna and Deepa stop speaking over?
qa.a: A borrowed laptop charger, or really what the charger meant.

qa.q: Why did Minakshi's stomach twist when each friend asked Minakshi to take a side?
qa.a: Part of Minakshi wanted to please whoever was in the room, even though Minakshi knew not to carry tales.

qa.q: What could someone in Minakshi's position say when both friends want them on their side?
qa.a: Say kindly that they will not carry messages or pick a side, keep their own view, and stay warm to both.

qa.q: Why might Bhavna and Deepa have trusted Minakshi later?
qa.a: Because Minakshi never repeated what either had said, each could tell Minakshi would not repeat their words to others either.

grounding: Two friends fall out and both want Minakshi on their side; Minakshi refuses to carry tales and stays kind to both.

passage:
Ramesh, come, sit. Both your friends calling you to take sides? Let me tell you about Kamla and Shobha.
It was 1981, our second year at college in Nagpur. Back then your Nani was just Vinita, a girl of twenty, eager to be liked. They ran a pickle stall together at the college fair, then quarrelled over the money box. Kamla would catch me after class: "You agree she cheated, na?" And I'd nod. In the evening Shobha would come to the hostel: "Kamla is so dramatic, isn't she?" And I'd nod again.
Of course they compared notes. For one terrible week, both of them stopped talking to me.
After that I made a rule. When Kamla complained, I said, "I won't carry this to Shobha, and I won't carry her words to you. You two should talk." I still had tea with both. I told each what I honestly thought, once, and didn't repeat it.
They made up by winter. I learned it by losing both for a week. You can learn it cheaper, beta.

qa.q: What did Kamla and Shobha quarrel over?
qa.a: The money box of their pickle stall at the college fair.

qa.q: How did Vinita feel during the week both friends stopped talking to her?
qa.a: Terrible and lonely, and ashamed that nodding along with each of them had been found out.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Vinita's story, and what changed after it?
qa.a: Losing both friends for a week; after that Vinita refused to carry tales, gave each friend an honest view once, and kept having tea with both.

qa.q: How might Kamla have felt on learning Vinita also agreed with Shobha?
qa.a: Betrayed and angry, feeling that Kamla's trust had been used by someone who only nodded along.

grounding: Shows being pulled between two quarrelling friends, the harm of agreeing with whoever is present, and refusing to carry tales while staying kind to both.

passage:
The surprise party for Kavita was at eight, the cake was still at the bakery across town, and Shreya and Tanmay weren't speaking. They'd fallen out over who would give the speech, and each had been calling Sachin all afternoon.
"You think Tanmay's being a control freak, right?" Shreya asked in the auto, balancing the balloons.
Sachin felt the easy answer rise: yeah, totally. He'd said exactly that to Tanmay about Shreya an hour earlier, just to end the call. His stomach twisted.
"Honestly? I think you both want this to be perfect for Kavita," he said. "I'm not going to repeat what either of you says about the other. I did that once today already, and it wasn't fair."
Shreya stared. "You told him I was annoying?"
"I agreed when he said it. I'm sorry. I'll tell him the same."
Traffic crawled. At the bakery, Sachin texted Tanmay and suggested they split the speech. By 7:55, both were holding the cake, not quite smiling, but side by side.

qa.q: What time was the surprise party for Kavita?
Why did Sachin's stomach twist in the auto?
qa.a: He felt guilty, remembering he had agreed with Tanmay about Shreya an hour earlier just to end the call.

qa.q: What did Sachin do to stop being caught in the middle?
qa.a: He refused to carry either friend's words, owned his earlier slip to Shreya, and suggested they split the speech.

qa.q: How might Shreya feel hearing Sachin admit he agreed with Tanmay?
qa.a: Stung at first, but more able to trust him because he told her the truth.

grounding: Illustrates two friends fighting and both wanting you on their side, and choosing not to carry tales while staying kind to both.
